findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables, committed to source control. Anyone with read access to the repository, the Terraform state, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve these long-lived credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables (which hold secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are readable in plaintext by any principal with lambda:GetFunction permissions, with no separate KMS key policy boundary.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to known unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary — enabling data exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function code is compromised.

No aws_lambda_permission or resource-based policy scoping is defined alongside the function, so invocation authorization depends entirely on external IAM grants; combined with the plaintext credentials in its configuration this widens the exposure surface.
